Fit a graph-structured multivariate covariance generalized linear model

Source: R/mcglm_graph.R, R/methods.R
mcglm_graph.Rd

Fits a multivariate covariance generalized linear model (MCGLM) and then estimates a graph-structured covariance for its Pearson residuals, in a two-stage residual analysis. The between-response covariance is parametrized either by a Gaussian graphical model (GGM, linear in the precision matrix) or by a directed acyclic graph (DAG, modified Cholesky factorization).

Usage

mcglm_graph(
  linear_pred,
  between_graph = mc_between_graph("ggm"),
  data,
  matrix_pred = NULL,
  control = list(),
  ...
)

mcglmgraph(
  linear_pred,
  between_graph = mc_between_graph("ggm"),
  data,
  matrix_pred = NULL,
  control = list(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mcglm_graph'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mcglm_graph'
summary(
  object,
  variability = c("model", "empirical", "two_stage"),
  cluster = NULL,
  small_sample = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mcglm_graph'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mcglm_graph'
coef(object, type = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mcglm_graph'
plot(x, type = c("network", "residuals"), ...)

Arguments

linear_pred

a list of model formulas, one per response; at least two responses are required.

between_graph

a specification from mc_between_graph (default: the GGM layer on the complete graph).

data

a data frame containing the variables in linear_pred. It must hold complete cases: a missing or non-finite response value, a missing covariate, or a non-finite offset, Ntrial or weights entry passed through ..., is refused with an error that names the response and the number of rows affected, because the graph layer needs one complete vector of Pearson residuals per unit. Removing or imputing incomplete rows is left to the user.

matrix_pred

optional list of within-response covariance bases, as in mcglm, one element per response. When NULL, an identity structure (mc_id) is used for every response.

control

a named list of control parameters for the between-response engine; unknown names are an error. The components are:

max_iter

maximum number of Newton iterations (default 100).

tol

tolerance on the relative parameter change \(\max_d |\theta_d^{(t+1)} - \theta_d^{(t)}| / (1 + |\theta_d^{(t)}|)\) between consecutive iterations, computed on \(\eta\) or on \((\gamma, \delta)\) (default 1e-8).

score_tol

bound on the maximum absolute value of the estimating function divided by \(n\) at the solution (default sqrt(tol)).

rcond_tol

smallest admissible reciprocal condition number of the sensitivity matrix; below it a ridge is used in linear solves and the fit is not certified (default .Machine$double.eps^(2/3)).

verbose

logical; report the iterations (default FALSE).

dag_solver

how the DAG layer is solved: "closed" (default) takes the node-by-node root of mc_dag_closed_root, and "newton" runs the scoring iteration shared with the GGM layer. The two solve the same equations, the first exactly and without iterating, and agree up to the convergence tolerance of the iteration; the closed route is much faster when the number of responses is large. It has no effect on the GGM layer, which has no closed root.

...

for mcglm_graph() and mcglmgraph(): further arguments passed to mcglm (such as link, variance, power_fixed, offset, Ntrial, weights). For the methods: ignored by the print methods and by plot with type = "residuals"; passed on to the inherited mcglm method by summary and coef; passed to mc_plot_network by plot with type = "network".

x

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

object

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

variability

for summary: the covariance of the graph parameters behind the standard errors, "model" (default), "empirical" for the sandwich or "two_stage", as in mc_vcov_graph. With "two_stage" the correction takes the route of method = "auto" there.

cluster, small_sample

for summary: passed to mc_vcov_graph; they apply to variability = "empirical" and "two_stage" only and are refused with "model".

type

for coef: optional, one of "regression", "graph" or "dispersion", or a type accepted by the mcglm method. For plot: "network" for the dependence network or "residuals" for residual histograms.

Value

An object of class c("mcglm_graph", "mcglm"). In addition to all the standard mcglm components, it carries a list $graph with the components

  • type, spec: the layer ("ggm" or "dag") and the canonical mc_between_graph specification, with the number of responses recorded;

  • par, vcov, J, npar, edge_pos: the named numeric vector of graph parameters (eta_kk then eta_ij for the GGM layer; gamma_ji, the coefficient of response \(i\) in the equation of response \(j\), then delta_j for the DAG layer), their model-based covariance \(J_n^{-1}\), the accumulated sensitivity matrix \(J_n\), the number of parameters, and the integer positions of the edge parameters in par. The matrix vcov carries the attributes "inversion_status" and "inversion_ridge";

  • Sigma_b, K_b: the fitted \(R \times R\) between-response covariance and precision, in the order of the responses;

  • Dlist: the list of npar matrices \(\dot\Sigma_{b,d}\), the derivatives of Sigma_b with respect to each element of par;

  • Shat, residuals, n, R, response_names: the empirical covariance of the Pearson residuals \(\hat S_e\), the \(n \times R\) matrix of residuals (not centered), the number of units and responses, and the response labels;

  • iter, converged, status, solver: the number of iterations (zero for the closed-form DAG solution), the logical convergence indicator, a status string ("converged" or "closed_form" for a certified fit, otherwise the reason why it is not, such as "max_iter", "spd_line_search_failed", "linear_solve_failed", "score_not_converged" or "sensitivity_ill_conditioned"), and the solver used ("newton" or "closed");

  • score_norm, score_norm_unit, rcond_J, score_tol, rcond_tol, convergence_gates, stopping_rule: the largest absolute coordinate of the estimating function at the solution (accumulated and divided by \(n\)), the reciprocal condition number of \(J_n\), the two thresholds, the named logical vector of the three conditions (parameter_change, score, sensitivity) and a character description of the rule, so that a fit stopped by the parameter-change rule can be checked against the size of the estimating function it leaves;

  • inversion_status, inversion_ridge, linear_solve_status, linear_solve_ridge, inference_ok: whether the inversion of \(J_n\) and the linear solves of the iterations were exact ("exact", or "exact_blockwise" for the closed-form DAG solution) or "ridge_regularized", the ridge added in each (zero when exact), and a logical that is TRUE when the inversion was exact and the three convergence conditions hold, in which case graph-layer inference is certified;

  • meta, init_info, control: a list of builder metadata (layer, numbers of responses, edges and parameters, and the bases of the GGM layer or the ordering and edge matrices of the DAG layer), the diagnostics of the starting value (a list for the DAG layer solved by Newton iterations, NULL otherwise) and the control list used.

A graph layer that did not converge is returned with a warning.

Details

First stage. The mean and within-response dispersion parameters are estimated by mcglm with the quasi-score and Pearson estimating functions of Bonat and Jorgensen (2016) doi:10.1111/rssc.12145 , under the usual correlation-based between-response structure of that package. The \(n \times R\) matrix \(E\) of Pearson residuals, with rows \(r_i^\top\), is then formed, and $$\hat S_e = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(r_i - \bar r)(r_i - \bar r)^\top$$ is its empirical covariance, centered at the column means \(\bar r\) and with divisor \(n\).

Second stage. The between-response covariance \(\Sigma_b\) with precision \(K_b = \Sigma_b^{-1}\) is estimated from \(\hat S_e\) by the second-order Pearson estimating function $$\psi_d(\theta) = -\frac{n}{2}\left\{ \mathrm{tr}(\Sigma_b^{-1} \dot\Sigma_{b,d}) - \mathrm{tr}(\Sigma_b^{-1} \dot\Sigma_{b,d} \Sigma_b^{-1} \hat S_e) \right\},\qquad \dot\Sigma_{b,d} = \partial\Sigma_b/\partial\theta_d,$$ whose sensitivity matrix, in the accumulated scale, has entries $$[J_n]_{da} = \frac{n}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma_b^{-1} \dot\Sigma_{b,d} \Sigma_b^{-1} \dot\Sigma_{b,a}).$$ The vector of graph parameters is \(\theta = \eta\) for the GGM layer, with \(K_b = \sum_d \eta_d Z_d\) (see mc_precision_bases), and \(\theta = (\gamma, \delta)\) for the DAG layer, with \(\Sigma_b = T^{-1} D T^{-\top}\) (see mc_between_graph). The order of the parameters within \(\theta\) is given in mc_build_sigma_between_graph. Both layers keep \(R\) free scale parameters, the diagonal of \(K_b\) or the innovation variances \(\delta\): \(\Sigma_b\) is the covariance of the Pearson residuals and is not normalized to a correlation matrix. Partial correlations and the support of the precision are unaffected by that scale.

In the GGM layer, \(\dot\Sigma_{b,d} = -\Sigma_b Z_d \Sigma_b\) reduces the two expressions to $$\psi_{\eta_d} = \frac{n}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}\{Z_d(\Sigma_b - \hat S_e)\}, \qquad [J_n]_{da} = \frac{n}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(Z_d \Sigma_b Z_a \Sigma_b),$$ so that the root matches \(\Sigma_b\) to \(\hat S_e\) on the diagonal and on the edges of the graph, which are the covariance selection equations of Dempster (1972). The equations are solved by Newton iterations \(\eta \leftarrow \eta + \alpha J_n^{-1}\psi\), started at the corresponding entries of \(\hat S_e^{-1}\), with the step \(\alpha\) halved from 1, at most 30 times, until the smallest eigenvalue of \(K_b\) exceeds \(10^{-10}\) (see mc_spd_line_search); when no such step is found the iteration stops at the current iterate with status "spd_line_search_failed". The DAG layer has a closed-form root, node by node (see mc_dag_closed_root), and can also be solved by Newton iterations on \((\gamma, \log\delta)\).

A fit is declared converged when three conditions hold: the relative change of the parameters in the last iteration falls below tol, the largest absolute coordinate of the estimating function, divided by \(n\), is at most score_tol, and the reciprocal condition number of the sensitivity matrix exceeds rcond_tol. The closed-form DAG solution takes no step, so there the first condition is replaced by the requirements that no innovation variance is floored and no parent block is ill-conditioned.

The graph layer is stored in $graph and does not replace the covariance components of the first-stage "mcglm" object. Consequently, inherited mcglm methods such as vcov, gof, pAIC, pBIC and plogLik refer to the first-stage fit; graph-specific results are exposed through the mc_* helpers. Because the graph layer is estimated from fitted residuals, its default (model-based) covariance does not account for the estimation of the first stage; see mc_vcov_graph for the corrected forms.

Methods (by generic)

  • print(mcglm_graph): Print the fit, highlighting the graph layer: the layer, the number of responses, units and edges, the convergence of the between-response engine and the between-response covariance \(\boldsymbol\Sigma_b\). Returns x invisibly.

  • summary(mcglm_graph): Summary combining the mcglm summary with the graph layer (graph parameters, partial correlations and information criteria). Returns an object of class "summary.mcglm_graph", a list with the first-stage summary in first_stage and its printed lines in first_stage_text; layer, R, n and n_edges; converged, status and inference_ok; the variability used; the data frame coefficients of the graph parameters, with columns Estimate, Std.Error, z (their ratio) and p.value (two-sided, standard normal reference, for the null value zero of each parameter taken alone), the last three NA when the fit is not certified for inference; partial_cor, the matrix of partial correlations; and criteria, the AIC, BIC and QIC of the graph layer. Its print method shows the first stage and then the graph layer, and returns its argument invisibly.

  • coef(mcglm_graph): Extract coefficients. With no type, or with a type of coef.mcglm ("beta", "tau", "power", "correlation"), the inherited mcglm method answers, with its arguments std.error and response passed through ..., and returns its data frame; otherwise type, which may be abbreviated, selects the regression, graph or dispersion coefficients, returned as plain numeric vectors.

  • plot(mcglm_graph): Diagnostic and network plots. With type = "network" it draws the dependence network with mc_plot_network and returns invisibly the matrix of edge weights that function returns; with type = "residuals" it draws one histogram of the Pearson residuals per response, restores the graphical parameters on exit and returns x invisibly.

Functions

  • print(summary.mcglm_graph): Print the summary: the first stage as mcglm prints it, then the graph layer.

Two spellings of the same function

mcglmgraph() and mcglm_graph() are the same object: the second name is bound to the first, not wrapped around it, so there is no forwarding layer and the two cannot drift apart. mcglmgraph() matches the package name and is the preferred spelling for new code; mcglm_graph() is kept for existing scripts. Neither is deprecated.

The class of the returned object is "mcglm_graph" under both spellings, and it is the class on which the S3 methods are registered.

References

Bonat, W. H. and Jorgensen, B. (2016). Multivariate covariance generalized linear models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied Statistics), 65(5), 649-675. doi:10.1111/rssc.12145

Dempster, A. P. (1972). Covariance selection. Biometrics, 28(1), 157-175. doi:10.2307/2528966

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Oxford University Press.

See also

mc_between_graph to specify the layer, mc_partial_cor, mc_partial_cor_delta and mc_get_graph to interpret it, mc_vcov_graph for the covariance of the graph parameters, and mc_build_sigma_between_graph for the map from the parameters to \(\Sigma_b\).

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 200; x <- rnorm(n)
y1 <- 1 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(n)
y2 <- 0.4 * y1 + 0.3 * x + rnorm(n)
y3 <- 0.2 * y2 + rnorm(n)
dat <- data.frame(y1, y2, y3, x)
fit <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x),
                   between_graph = mc_between_graph("ggm"), data = dat)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
fit
#> Multivariate Covariance GLM with graph-structured between-response covariance
#> Layer: GGM | responses: 3 | n: 200 | edges: 3
#> Between-response engine converged: TRUE (1 iterations)
#> 
#> Between-response covariance (Sigma_b):
#>        y1     y2     y3
#> y1 0.9900 0.3303 0.0632
#> y2 0.3303 0.9900 0.1647
#> y3 0.0632 0.1647 0.9900
#> 
#> This is also a valid 'mcglm' object: use coef(), vcov(), gof(), ...
coef(fit)            # inherited mcglm method
#>      Estimates Parameters        Type Response
#> 1   1.04145787     beta10        beta        1
#> 2   0.47692216     beta11        beta        1
#> 3   0.37196615     beta20        beta        2
#> 4   0.56927839     beta21        beta        2
#> 5  -0.02812858     beta30        beta        3
#> 6   0.19431290     beta31        beta        3
#> 7   0.33358711      rho12 correlation       NA
#> 8   0.06386570      rho13 correlation       NA
#> 9   0.16631396      rho23 correlation       NA
#> 10  1.02622172      tau11         tau        1
#> 11  1.28803308      tau21         tau        2
#> 12  1.22256601      tau31         tau        3
mc_partial_cor(fit)  # graph layer
#>             y1        y2          y3
#> y1 1.000000000 0.3281972 0.009020603
#> y2 0.328197212 1.0000000 0.154134931
#> y3 0.009020603 0.1541349 1.000000000
